Sam —

Thanks — great questions. Short answers below; I attached a one‑page residency & deletion summary as well (Redwood_HostedAPI_Residency_Summary.pdf). If you want a deeper technical writeup we can loop in Engineering but this should be sufficient for your questionnaire.

1) Data residency
- Default behavior: For our hosted API, request payloads and generated outputs are processed in the region selected at account creation and stored transiently in that region only. We do not replicate customer request/response payloads across regions by default.
- Regional control: Customers can request region-lock during provisioning (e.g., us-west-2). For regulated accounts we offer geo-restriction controls in the account settings — we will record a region lock and route all traffic to that region.
- Note: Model parameters (the model binaries) are cached on multi-region GPU fleets for performance but are not tenant-specific data and do not contain customer inputs.

2) Retention & deletion
- Default retention: Interaction logs (request/response text and derived artifacts such as embeddings) are retained for 30 days by default for monitoring and quality purposes. Audit logs (metadata about API calls) are retained for 365 days.
- Customer controls: Enterprise customers can configure retention windows per-account (minimum 0 days / maximum 3650 days) when on a Dedicated or Private plan; for Hosted accounts we can set custom retention policies via a support request and a data addendum.
- Account erasure workflow: Upon a verified erasure request we start a phased removal: (a) mark records for purge and stop including them in any analytics pipelines (within 24 hours), (b) delete primary records from active storage (within 72 hours), (c) remove from nearline backups / caches and run a background scrub (30 days), and (d) confirm completion and provide a summary report (typically within 30 calendar days).
- Backups: Backups are encrypted and retention-bound; customer data may persist in immutable backup snapshots for a limited retention period (by default up to 30 days). We provide a certified attestation for customers that need backup purge evidence — exceptions must be scoped in contract.

3) Evidence & attestations
- Attached: Redwood_HostedAPI_Residency_Summary.pdf — one-page summary of region controls, retention defaults, and erasure workflow.
- For formal audits: we can provide SOC 2 artifacts and a redacted deletion playbook under NDA or as part of our compliance pack.

If Delta needs stricter guarantees (region lock + accelerated purge) we can add contractual language to the SOW. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the spreadsheet rows.
